title_en: Gao v. People's Government of Zhao County, Hebei Province — administrative compensation dispute
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 27, Paragraph 2, and Article 32 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases, where land or houses are illegally expropriated or requisitioned, the administrative compensation awarded by the people's court to the expropriated person shall not be less than the resettlement and indemnity rights and interests that the expropriated person is entitled to according to law. Where the losses of the expropriated person have been fully remedied through other channels such as administrative indemnity, no further support shall be given in the administrative compensation case.
keywords_en: administrative; administrative compensation; retrial; Supreme People's Court; Hebei Province; natural person; state organ; State Compensation Law; Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases; relationship between administrative compensation and administrative indemnity; compensation standard for illegal forced demolition of houses; legality review of the decision to deny compensation; reversal on appeal; shantytown renovation; forced demolition of houses; retrieval of homestead land; application for administrative compensation; no double support for indemnity and compensation; application for retrial
full_text_en:
高某诉河北省赵县人民政府行政赔偿案

【Ruling Summary】

According to Article 27, Paragraph 2 and Article 32 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases, where land or houses are illegally expropriated or requisitioned, the administrative compensation awarded by the people's court to the expropriated party shall not be less than the resettlement compensation rights and interests that the expropriated party is entitled to receive according to law. If the losses of the expropriated party have been fully remedied through other channels such as administrative compensation, such losses shall no longer be supported in the administrative compensation case.

However, if the relevant legitimate rights and interests of the expropriated party have not yet been remedied through compensation channels, and the house has been forcibly demolished and the demolition act has been confirmed illegal according to law, the expropriated party may seek relief through compensation channels according to law. If the compensation obligor makes a decision to deny compensation and informs the party that compensation funds have been reserved and can be collected by signing a resettlement compensation agreement, such decision does not comply with the provisions of laws and judicial interpretations. If the administrative organ makes a compensation decision during the compensation litigation process, because the compensation decision is a new administrative act and not a change to the challenged decision to deny compensation, the people's court shall still examine the legality of the decision to deny compensation and render a judgment. In accordance with the principle that overlapping parts of compensation and indemnity are not to be supported repeatedly, if a loss has already been remedied through compensation channels, the claim for compensation shall not be supported according to law.

Administrative Compensation Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2024) Zui Gao Fa Xing Zai No. 38

Re-applicant (plaintiff at first instance, appellant at second instance): Gao, residing in Zhao County, Hebei Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Chuanxue, lawyer of Beijing Shengting Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Chang Xiaohui, lawyer of Beijing Shengting Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance, appellee at second instance): Zhao County People's Government of Hebei Province. Domicile: Zhao County, Hebei Province.

Legal representative: Huang, County Chief.

Agent ad litem: Zhang, staff member of Zhao County Natural Resources and Planning Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Zhu, staff member of Zhao County Minsheng Legal Service Office.

Re-applicant Gao, in connection with the administrative compensation dispute against the respondent Zhao County People's Government of Hebei Province (hereinafter referred to as Zhao County Government), filed a petition for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the Administrative Compensation Judgment (2022) Ji Xing Pei Zhong No. 58 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court. This Court, by the Administrative Compensation Ruling (2023) Zui Gao Fa Xing Pei Shen No. 236 dated December 29, 2023, decided to bring the case for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and has now concluded the trial.

The first instance, the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province, found that Gao was a villager of Dongmou Village, Zhaozhou Town, Zhao County, and together with her husband Chen A (deceased), owned a lawful homestead and above-ground houses in the village. In 2018, Dongmou Village was included in a national shantytown renovation project. On May 8, 2018, the Zhao County Government issued the "Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan for the Dongmou Village Urban Village Shantytown Renovation Project in Zhao County" (hereinafter referred to as the "Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan"). On May 16, 2019, the Dongmou Village Committee initiated legal procedures to recover Gao's homestead. On May 21, the Dongmou Village Committee recovered Gao's homestead. On May 22, the Dongmou Village Committee issued a decision ordering Gao to vacate within five days from receipt of the decision, failing which forced eviction would be carried out. Gao did not voluntarily vacate within the specified time limit. On May 28, 2019, Gao's house was forcibly demolished by the Zhao County Government. Subsequently, Gao filed an administrative lawsuit with this court, which, by Administrative Judgment (2021) Ji 01 Xing Chu No. 13 dated February 7, 2021, confirmed that the Zhao County Government's organization of the forced demolition of Gao's house was illegal. The Zhao County Government appealed to the Hebei High People's Court. On August 26, 2021, the Hebei High People's Court rendered Administrative Judgment (2021) Ji Xing Zhong No. 586, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. On November 29, 2021, Gao filed a state compensation application with the Zhao County Government. On January 25, 2022, the Zhao County Government issued Zhao Zheng Pei Jue Zi (2022) No. 6, a decision to deny administrative compensation, denying Gao's state compensation application. The decision to deny compensation stated: The subject homestead of Gao had been lawfully recovered by the Dongmou Village Committee, and the demolished house could not be restored to its original condition. Before the demolition, the subject house had been appraised, and the compensation funds were stored in a special account, from which Gao could sign and collect at any time; the homestead could be exchanged in accordance with the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan, and Gao's legitimate rights and interests were fully protected without damage. Article 2 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC provides that where state organs or their personnel, in exercising their functions and powers, commit any act that infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen, legal person, or other organization as provided by this Law, causing damage, the victim has the right to obtain state compensation in accordance with this Law. In this case, although the people's court confirmed that the Zhao County Government's organization of the forced demolition of Gao's house was illegal, the act did not cause damage to her legitimate rights and interests. Gao's application did not fall within the scope of administrative compensation. After fully hearing Gao's opinions and failing to reach an agreement through consultation, the authority decided, in accordance with Articles 13 and 14 of the State Compensation Law of the PRC, to deny Gao's state compensation application.

It was further found that Gao had previously filed an administrative lawsuit against the recovery of the old homestead. This court, by Administrative Judgment (2019) Ji 01 Xing Chu No. 171, dismissed Gao's claims. Gao appealed to the Hebei High People's Court. On September 27, 2020, the Hebei High People's Court rendered Administrative Judgment (2020) Ji Xing Zhong No. 581, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

The Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province held in the first instance that this case was an administrative compensation lawsuit filed by Gao based on the confirmation that the Zhao County Government's act of forcibly demolishing the house on the subject homestead was illegal. Although the forcible demolition act had been confirmed illegal by an effective judgment, the subject homestead of Gao met the compensation and resettlement requirements of the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan, and the Zhao County Government had already reserved demolition compensation funds, relocation exchange houses, and related expenses for Gao, and Gao could sign a resettlement compensation agreement and collect at any time. Therefore, Gao's compensation claim for the forcibly demolished subject house could be realized by signing a resettlement compensation agreement. Gao's request for compensation from the Zhao County Government was not supported by this court. Additionally, Gao did not submit effective evidence of the loss of items inside the forcibly demolished house, and this compensation claim lacked factual basis. In conclusion, in accordance with Article 32, Item 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases, the court dismissed Gao's claims.

The Hebei High People's Court further found in the second instance that another party in a separate case, Chen B, dissatisfied with the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan, had filed an administrative lawsuit with the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province. The Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court rendered Administrative Judgment (2020) Ji 01 Xing Chu No. 75, dismissing Chen B's claims. Chen B appealed, and the Hebei High People's Court rendered Administrative Judgment (2021) Ji Xing Zhong No. 87, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

The Hebei High People's Court held in the second instance that the right to use the homestead involved in the case had been approved for recovery by the village collective by the Zhao County Government in accordance with legal procedures. The effective judgment of the people's court confirmed that the Zhao County Government's act of approving the recovery of the homestead was lawful, and another effective judgment also confirmed the legality of the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan. Although the forcible demolition act by the Zhao County Government had been confirmed illegal by an effective judgment, the subject homestead of Gao met the compensation and resettlement requirements of the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan, and the Zhao County Government had clearly stated in the decision to deny administrative compensation that, before demolition, the subject house had been appraised by an appraisal company, the compensation funds were stored in a special account, and Gao could sign and collect at any time; the homestead could be exchanged in accordance with the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan. Accordingly, Gao's compensation claim for the forcibly demolished subject house could be fully remedied through administrative compensation channels. According to Article 32, Item 3 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases, the first-instance judgment dismissing her claims was correct in result and should be upheld. In conclusion, in accordance with Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the appeal was dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

Gao petitioned for retrial, arguing: (1) The first-instance judgment's finding that "the Zhao County Government had already reserved demolition compensation funds, relocation exchange houses, and related expenses for Gao, and Gao could sign a resettlement compensation agreement and collect at any time" was unclear in factual determination; (2) Her various compensation claims were reasonable, lawful, and should be supported. Therefore, she requested the revocation of the first-instance and second-instance compensation judgments and a retrial or remand for retrial.

The Zhao County Government responded, arguing: (1) On December 28, 2023, it had already issued to the re-applicant the "Zhao County People's Government Compensation and Resettlement Decision," which provided comprehensive compensation for the re-applicant's due benefits in accordance with the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan, and additionally granted interest compensation. The re-applicant's compensation claims had been fully remedied through administrative compensation channels. (2) The re-applicant had filed a lawsuit in July 2019 against the Zhao County Government's administrative act of approving the recovery of the right to use the homestead. The effective judgment affirmed the legality of the Dongmou Village urban village shantytown renovation project and that the Dongmou Village Committee's application for recovery of the right to use the homestead was for the public interest of the villagers, and the act of approving the recovery of the subject right to use the homestead complied with legal provisions. (3) The right to use the subject homestead had been lawfully recovered by the collective economic organization. The effective judgment of the people's court confirmed that the act of recovering the land and the compensation and resettlement plan were lawful and effective. The re-applicant had no reason to refuse to sign the agreement. Any losses resulting from such refusal, such as signing bonuses and interest, should be borne by the re-applicant herself. Therefore, the application for retrial should be dismissed.

During the retrial of this case, the Zhao County Government submitted to this Court the compensation and resettlement decision issued to Gao's household on December 28, 2023, and the receipt of service dated January 21, 2024. The main contents of the decision: The homestead area of 207.9 sqm was to be exchanged for 207.9 sqm of resettlement housing, with the principles for area expansion, price difference settlement, etc., to be executed in accordance with the Demolition Compensation and Resettlement Plan; the building area of 215.36 sqm was to serve as the calculation basis for relevant compensation items; the replacement value of above-ground structures was RMB 152,640; compensation for decoration, finishing, and attachments was RMB 32,506; moving subsidy was RMB 1,600; relocation fee for indoor and outdoor facilities was RMB 250; total above: RMB 186,996; interest: interest on the above amounts was to be calculated from the date of demolition of the house, July 9, 2019, until the date of full payment of the compensation amounts, at the one-year benchmark interest rate for lump-sum deposits and withdrawals published by the People's Bank of China at the time of making the compensation decision, using bank interest calculation methods; temporary resettlement fee was RMB 83,068 (provisionally calculated from July 9, 2019, the date of demolition, to December 28, 2023; the actual amount to be calculated based on the time of house delivery). Gao's household had already received the above compensation and resettlement decision.

This Court held in the retrial that Article 27, Paragraph 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Compensation Cases provides that where land or houses are illegally expropriated or requisitioned, the administrative compensation awarded by the people's court to the expropriated party shall not be less than the resettlement compensation rights and interests that the expropriated party is entitled to receive according to law. Article 32 provides that a people's court shall dismiss the plaintiff's claim for administrative compensation under any of the following circumstances: (1) the damage claimed by the plaintiff has no factual basis; (2) the damage claimed by the plaintiff has no causal relationship with the illegal administrative act; (3) the plaintiff's losses have been fully remedied through other channels such as administrative compensation; (4) other circumstances where the plaintiff's grounds for requesting administrative compensation are untenable. In this case, the re-applicant's house was forcibly demolished, and an effective judgment confirmed the illegality of the Zhao County Government's forcible demolition act. The re-applicant applied to the Zhao County Government for administrative compensation. The Zhao County Government should bear administrative compensation liability according to law, and should adhere to the standard that compensation shall not be less than indemnity, so as to fully cover the re-applicant's losses. However, both the Zhao County Government's decision to deny compensation and the first-instance and second-instance administrative compensation judgments considered that the case should be resolved through compensation channels, and until the re-applicant petitioned this Court for retrial, the Zhao County Government had neither reached a compensation agreement with the re-applicant nor issued a compensation and resettlement decision. Therefore, this case did not fall under the circumstance provided by the judicial interpretation that a claim may be dismissed where the loss has been remedied through compensation. The Zhao County Government's decision to deny compensation and the first-instance and second-instance administrative compensation judgments lacked factual and legal basis and should be revoked. Although the Zhao County Government issued a compensation and resettlement decision to Gao's household during the retrial period, this act was a new administrative act, not a change to the challenged decision to deny compensation, and did not fall under the circumstance of "the defendant changed the original illegal administrative act" as provided in Article 74, Paragraph 2, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC. This Court shall still examine the legality of the challenged decision to deny compensation and render a judgment.

Regarding whether specific compensation items and amounts should be adjudicated in this case: Given that during the retrial period, the respondent made a compensation and resettlement decision, clarifying the items, scope, method, and amounts of compensation and resettlement for the demolished house, and the re-applicant's compensation claim was limited to house losses without including movable property losses, and no evidence was submitted to prove the loss of indoor items, the compensation issue in this case has been resolved through compensation channels. In accordance with the principle of no repeated relief, where losses have been fully covered through compensation channels, the claim for compensation may be denied. If the re-applicant has objections to the compensation and resettlement decision, she may seek relief separately according to law.

In conclusion, in accordance with Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 119, Paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the Administrative Compensation Judgment (2022) Ji Xing Pei Zhong No. 58 of the Hebei High People's Court;
2. Revoke the Administrative Compensation Judgment (2022) Ji 01 Xing Pei Chu No. 4 of the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province;
3. Revoke Zhao Zheng Pei Jue Zi (2022) No. 6, the Decision to Deny Administrative Compensation of Zhao County People's Government of Hebei Province;
4. Dismiss Gao's claims for administrative compensation.

This judgment is final.
